solution: The sentence establishes a contrast between realism (theories provide true descriptions) and instrumentalism (theories are merely useful tools). The blank describes instrumentalists' view of the ontological claims (claims about what exists) made by theories. Since instrumentalists see theories only as predictive tools, they would view ontological claims as lacking genuine content or being misleading. 'Vacuous' (empty of meaning or substance) and 'specious' (superficially plausible but actually wrong) both capture this instrumentalist skepticism. 'Veridical' (truthful) contradicts the instrumentalist position. 'Heuristic' (serving as a guide to discovery) doesn't capture the negative evaluation of ontological claims. 'Epiphenomenal' (secondary byproduct) is too specific and doesn't fit the context. 'Corroborative' (confirming) is opposite to the required meaning.
